أَسْوَدُ صَالِخٌ i. q. أَسْوَدُ سَالِخٌ [q. v.], A certain species of serpents, that casts off its slough. (AHát, L.) ―
-b2- And جَرَبٌ صَالِخٌ i. q. سَالِخٌ [i. e. Excoriating mange or scab]: (K, TA:) it is such as occurs in the hinder part of the camel, and one doubts not its extending over the whole of his body. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
